# future.callr: Parallel Future Backend using ‘callr’

## Introduction

The **[future.callr](https://future.callr.futureverse.org)** package is
a backend for the **[future](https://future.futureverse.org)**
framework, also known as the [Futureverse](https://www.futureverse.org).
The Futureverse makes it easy to parallelize existing R code - often
with only a minor change of code. Most users interact with it via
higher-level packages such as
**[futurize](https://futurize.futureverse.org)**,
**[future.apply](https://future.apply.futureverse.org)**,
**[furrr](https://furrr.futureverse.org)**, and
**[doFuture](https://doFuture.futureverse.org)**, and you choose *where*
and *how* the code runs by setting a future backend with
[`plan()`](https://future.futureverse.org/reference/plan.html). This
package adds the `callr` backend, which runs each future in a fresh
background R process on the local machine using the
**[callr](https://cran.r-project.org/package=callr)** package.

\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`futurize`](https://futurize.futureverse.org)`)`\
[`plan`](https://future.futureverse.org/reference/plan.html)`(``future.callr``::`[`callr`](https://future.callr.futureverse.org/reference/callr.md)`)``  ``# parallelize on the current machine`\
\
`# A slow function`\
`slow_fcn`` ``<-`` ``function``(``x``)`` ``{`\
`  `[`Sys.sleep`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Sys.sleep.html)`(``1.0``)`\
`  ``x``^``2`\
`}`\
\
`# Example data`\
`xs`` ``<-`` ``1``:``10`\
\
`# Sequential and parallel base R apply`\
`ys`` ``<-`` `[`lapply`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/lapply.html)`(``xs``, ``slow_fcn``)`\
`ys`` ``<-`` `[`lapply`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/lapply.html)`(``xs``, ``slow_fcn``)`` ``|>`` `[`futurize`](https://futurize.futureverse.org/reference/futurize.html)`(``)`\
\
`# Sequential and parallel purrr map`\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`purrr`](https://purrr.tidyverse.org/)`)`\
`ys`` ``<-`` ``xs`` ``|>`` `[`map`](https://purrr.tidyverse.org/reference/map.html)`(``slow_fcn``)`\
`ys`` ``<-`` ``xs`` ``|>`` `[`map`](https://purrr.tidyverse.org/reference/map.html)`(``slow_fcn``)`` ``|>`` `[`futurize`](https://futurize.futureverse.org/reference/futurize.html)`(``)`\
\
`# Sequential and parallel foreach calls`\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`foreach`](https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/foreach)`)`\
`ys`` ``<-`` `[`foreach`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/foreach/man/foreach.html)`(``x ``=`` ``xs``)`` `[`%do%`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/foreach/man/foreach.html)` ``slow_fcn``(``x``)`\
`ys`` ``<-`` `[`foreach`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/foreach/man/foreach.html)`(``x ``=`` ``xs``)`` `[`%do%`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/foreach/man/foreach.html)` ``slow_fcn``(``x``)`` ``|>`` `[`futurize`](https://futurize.futureverse.org/reference/futurize.html)`(``)`

The only thing that differs from using [any other future
backend](https://www.futureverse.org/backends.html) is the
[`plan()`](https://future.futureverse.org/reference/plan.html) call. The
code does not have to change, it gives identical results, and it behaves
exactly the same.

## The callr backend

| Backend | Description | Alternative in future package |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `callr` | parallel evaluation in a separate R process (on current machine) | `plan(multisession)` |

Each `callr` future is resolved in a fresh background R process, which
ends as soon as the value of the future has been collected. In contrast,
`multisession` futures are resolved by R workers that stay alive and
serve many futures over their life spans.

### Advantages

- Each future starts from a clean R session. Futures cannot affect each
  other via memory allocations, finalizers, modified options, or loaded
  and attached packages.

- More than 125 futures can run in parallel. The `multisession` and
  `cluster` backends use one R connection per worker, and R has a
  default limit of 125 connections per session. **callr** does not use R
  connections, so this limit does not apply.

- No ports are used, which means there are no port clashes with other
  processes, and no firewall alerts on Windows.

### Limitations

- Launching a new R process for each future adds overhead. This makes
  the `callr` backend less suited for many small futures, where
  `plan(multisession)` might be faster.

- The R processes always run on the local machine. For workers on other
  machines, or on a high-performance compute (HPC) cluster, use another
  future backend, e.g. `plan(cluster)` or
  **[future.batchtools](https://future.batchtools.futureverse.org)**.

## Installation

R package future.callr is available on
[CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=future.callr) and can be
installed in R as:

\
[`install.packages`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/install.packages.html)`(``"future.callr"``)`

### Pre-release version

To install the pre-release version, use:

\
[`install.packages`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/install.packages.html)`(``"future.callr"``, repos ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"https://futureverse-devel.r-universe.dev"``, ``"https://cloud.r-project.org"``)``)`
